newsitem.title: INDIA: Asian firms, nations unite to speed core projects.
newsitem.headline: Asian firms, nations unite to speed core projects.

text.p: More than a dozen Asian countries will team up with private firms to launch a forum to speed up investment in core projects across the region, delegates to an infrastructure conference said on Monday.

They said the Asia Infrastructure Development Alliance (AIDA) would be launched later on Monday, the first day of a four-day meeting of the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) in the Indian capital.
AIDA will seek support from governments and the private sector to fund the region's huge infrastructure needs, they said.

"AIDA will take up issues relevant for increasing the pace of investment, particularly from the private sector, in Asian infrastructure projects," Graham Galloway, chairman of the consultancy firm Infrastructure Development Group, told Reuters.
A unit of his group, the Development Forum Administrators Pte Ltd, has been appointed as AIDA's secretariat, he said.

Galloway said some 18 countries were expected to join AIDA immediately. Private sector participants include Coopers and Lybrand, North West Water International, Microsoft, PowerGen , Linklaters and Paines, Lend Lease Capital Services and Gazprom.
"The role of the private sector in most other bodies is usually confined to that of an observer. Private sector members in AIDA will have equal status to government members," he said.
ESCAP estimates developing countries in the Asia-Pacific region need $1.5 trillion in core sector development between 1993 and 2000, of which $500 billion has been committed.
Galloway said AIDA would set up a detailed database of people and organisations for infrastructure development in the participating countries.
"The database will also have details about infrastructure, environment and regulations governing various sectors. It will be an easy route to information," Galloway said.
Some 30 Asian countries are participating in the ESCAP conference, which is aimed at improving the transport, communication and infrastructure facilities of developing nations.
AIDA's launch will coincide with the unveiling of a list of Asian-Pacific infrastructure projects open to private investors that was formulated last week by officials from ESCAP member countries.
